newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends weaker, U.S. dlr seen the key.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends weaker, U.S. dlr seen the key.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed little changed from its opening on Friday, easing back from its highs on a combination of the recovery of the U.S. dollar and weak local retail sales data.
It closed at US$0.0.6956/63 from its 0.6962/69 opening and after trading a 0.6957-75 range.
Dealers said the key to direction would be the U.S. dollar and there were hints that the big dollar could recover further after its battering earlier in the week.
"If that's the case then maybe the kiwi will struggle to make any significant upside," a chief dealer said.
The 3.9 percent fall in NZ March retail sales was well received by debt markets which saw interest rate yields ease back, and that is seen making the kiwi less attractive.
The Trade-Weighted Index was supported by the dollar's rebound. It ended at 67.78 from its 67.71 opening.
The index was seen well supported at 67.50 and could even retest 68.0, dealers said.
